key_insight: AgentRx shows that systematically annotating failed AI agent executions with a grounded, cross-domain failure taxonomy makes it possible to localize the critical failure step in long-horizon, noisy, multi-agent runs. The released benchmark of 115 annotated failed trajectories enables reproducible diagnosis and analysis.
problem_solved: Agents fail in ways that are hard to localize and study because runs are probabilistic, long-horizon, involve multiple agents/tools, and produce noisy outputs—AgentRx provides a structured dataset and taxonomy to identify where and why failures occur.
method: Manually annotate 115 failed agent execution trajectories spanning structured API workflows, incident management, and open-ended web/file tasks.
Derive a grounded-theory, cross-domain failure taxonomy and label each trajectory with its critical failure step and category.
Release the benchmark (AgentRx) to support reproducible diagnosis, analysis, and tool development for agent failures.
impact: Provides practitioners and researchers a concrete dataset and taxonomy to pinpoint failure causes, accelerate debugging of complex agent systems, and benchmark improvements in agent reliability and monitoring.
visual_elements: Annotated trajectory timeline: a horizontal flow showing actions/tools with the critical failure step highlighted in red.
Failure taxonomy tree: hierarchical diagram mapping categories to example failure modes (e.g., tool noise, planning error, communication mismatch).
Domain coverage chart: bar or donut chart showing the distribution of the 115 trajectories across the three task domains.
Example case study panel: side-by-side before/after snippets of a failed run with the annotated cause and suggested mitigation.
paper_title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
paper_authors: Shraddha Barke, Arnav Goyal, Alind Khare, Avaljot Singh, Suman Nath
